article_text:
The music of “ Michael ” is bringing some drama.

Variety has confirmed that Lionsgate’s bid to have its Michael Jackson biopic compete as a comedy or musical at the Golden Globes has been denied. News of the decision was first reported by Gold Derby.

The Golden Globes’ decision means the film, starring Jaafar Jackson as the King of Pop, is currently slated for the drama categories where it would compete for one of the six available slots against Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Los Javis’ “La Bola Negra” and more. The supporting actor and actress categories do not separate by genre, so this has no effect on his co-stars Colman Domingo and Nia Long.

Related Stories

Brandi Carlile to Receive Humanitarian Honor at National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards

Variety Nominated for 62 Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards

Lionsgate can appeal the ruling ahead of the Oct. 30 submission deadline. If the studio moves forward, the organization’s awards committee would evaluate the appeal. According to the Golden Globes rules, it states: “A musical can be a comedy or a drama in which songs are used in addition to spoken dialogue to further the plot.”

Under Globes procedure, when a film submits in a category that goes against the grain, or one in which it would not typically be accepted, a letter from the director is required to proceed. That letter, from “Michael” director Antoine Fuqua, was included with the studio’s submission. The organization reviewed the request and denied it anyway. An appeal may still be possible before the Oct. 30 submission deadline, but sources have shared that it will likely not be pursued. Lionsgate declined to comment.

Musical biopics have long been tricky to classify at the Globes. “Ray” and “Walk the Line” both competed in, and won, the comedy or musical categories in the mid-2000s. Those victories prompted a rule change requiring that songs propel the narrative rather than appear as standalone performances. In other words, music alone is no longer enough to qualify a film as a musical. By that standard, “Bohemian Rhapsody,” “Elvis,” and “A Complete Unknown” were all submitted as dramas in the years since. One notable exception: “Inside Llewyn Davis,” the Coen brothers’ story of a folk singer struggling for success in 1961, was permitted to compete as a comedy during its respective year.

That same distinction appears to have decided the fate of “Michael.” Jackson performs many of his uncle’s biggest hits in the film. Still, the organization evidently viewed those sequences as re-creations of Michael Jackson’s performances rather than as integral storytelling devices.

Fuqua’s film, which opened April 24, became the first biopic in history to surpass $1 billion at the worldwide box office and is Lionsgate’s biggest release ever. It also made a star of Jaafar Jackson , who had never acted professionally before.

The ruling does not affect the Globes’ broader slate of classification decisions. The awards show has accepted both “Obsession” and “Tender Loving Care” as comedies for consideration.

The 84th Golden Globe nominations will be announced Monday, Dec. 7, and the ceremony, hosted by Nikki Glaser, is set for Sunday, Jan. 10.

article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "It’s time to head back to Arrakis and the world of “Dune.”"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Both of Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune” movies will re-released in Imax theaters next month with an exclusive sneak peek at December’s “Dune: Part 3.” A double feature of both movies will hit Imax theaters on Nov. 13 only, with additional showtimes of each blockbuster film from Nov. 14-18."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Dune: Part 3” releases in theaters on Dec. 18 and is the long-awaited finale to Villeneuve’s epic sci-fi trilogy, starring Timothee Chalamet , Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Javier Bardem and more A-listers. article_text:
It’s time to head back to Arrakis and the world of “Dune.”

Both of Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune” movies will re-released in Imax theaters next month with an exclusive sneak peek at December’s “Dune: Part 3.” A double feature of both movies will hit Imax theaters on Nov. 13 only, with additional showtimes of each blockbuster film from Nov. 14-18.

“Dune: Part 3” releases in theaters on Dec. 18 and is the long-awaited finale to Villeneuve’s epic sci-fi trilogy, starring Timothee Chalamet , Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson, Jason Momoa, Florence Pugh, Javier Bardem and more A-listers. The new movie introduces Robert Pattinson as Scytale, shape-shifting villain who attempts to kill and overthrow Chalamet’s space emperor Paul Atreides. Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, the son of star Jason Momoa, and Ida Brooke will play Leto II Atreides and Ghanima Atreides, the twin children of Paul Atreides and Zendaya’s Chani. After appearing in a cameo in “Part 2,” Anya Taylor-Joy will return to play Alia Atreides, the younger sister of Paul. “Part 3” jumps ahead 20 years as Paul has conquered most of the universe and faces new threats.

Related Stories

The Muppets Turn 50 This Year but They Nearly Didn't Get Made at All: 'It Was a Real Study in Perseverance'

The first “Dune” movie, released in 2021, was nominated for 10 Oscars and went on to win six, including original score, sound, editing, cinematography, production design and visual effects. It was also up for best picture and adapted screenplay. The 2024 sequel won Oscars for best sound and visual effects out of its five nominations, which again included best picture. Both of the movies have been major box office hits for Warner Bros. and Legendary, with the first movie making $411 million worldwide and “Part 2” growing to $715 million.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "由于该市预告将再次爆发抗议活动，巴黎巴塞尔艺术展采取了史无前例的举措，缩短了今年的展期，周六和周日将闭馆。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "鉴于原定于周六在巴黎举行的再次游行示威，展会将于周五晚间提前闭幕——展会在一份声明中表示，此举是“出于保障我们的访客、参展商、合作伙伴、员工以及艺术品安全的利益”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "今年的展会自始至终笼罩在法国首都危机的阴影下。上周末，中学生及其他群体针对教育系统不公及其他社会弊端举行的抗题游行演变成暴力冲突。抵达巴黎的巴黎巴塞尔艺术展参展商和来宾在街头看到了冒烟的烧毁自行车堆和碎玻璃，以及无数被砸碎的窗户——不仅香榭丽舍大街上从迪奥（Dior）到拉科斯特（Lacoste）等奢侈品店遭遇破坏，连运动鞋店和隔壁的面包店也未能幸免。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "周二和周三的VIP预展日依然非常成功。据展会负责人卡里姆·克里帕（Karim Crippa）透露，尽管个别收藏家取消了行程，但展会的整体参观人数非常可观。不过早在周三就有传言称，出于对遭到蓄意破坏的担忧，大皇宫（Grand Palais）门前公共空间的艺术品可能会提前撤展。例如，艺术家阿利恰·克瓦德（Alicja Kwade）的一座高约4米半、由来自世界各地的抛光天然石球堆叠而成的塔楼“L’Élévation des Mondes”已确定于周五撤展，这位艺术家向《Monopol》证实了这一点——尽管克瓦德也表示，这些石球其实并不容易损坏。", "links": [{"text": "Messechef Karim Crippa", "url": "https://www.monopol-magazin.de/karim-crippa-art-basel-paris"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "参展商面临潜在的营业额损失", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在一封内部信中，展会方要求参展商在周五展会正式闭幕的19点之前，完整保留展馆内展位的展示，并宣布将为提前撤展提供后勤协助。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于参展商而言，展会叫停一方面意味着潜在的营业额损失，不过绝大多数销售额无论如何都在正式开幕前的几天内完成。展会本身则将失去通常参观人数众多的公众日的门票收入。同时，公众参观也将缺少两天开放时间。因此，本届巴黎巴塞尔艺术展实际上在很大程度上仅限艺术业内人士参与——这也是一个令人遗憾的副作用。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Wegen angekündigter erneuter Proteste in der Stadt verkürzt die Art Basel Paris in einem beispiellosen Vorgang ihre diesjährige Ausgabe und bleibt am Samstag und Sonntag geschlossen

Angesichts der für Samstag geplanten neuerlichen Demonstrationen in Paris schließt die Messe bereits am Freitagabend – "im Interesse der Sicherheit unserer Besucher, Aussteller, Partner, Mitarbeiter und der Kunstwerke", heißt es in einer Mitteilung der Messe.

Die diesjährige Ausgabe hatte von Anfang an im Zeichen der Krise in Frankreichs Hauptstadt gestanden. Am vergangenen Wochenende waren Demonstrationen von Schülerinnen und Schülern sowie anderen Gruppen gegen Ungerechtigkeiten im Bildungssystem und weitere soziale Missstände in Gewalt eskaliert. Die angereisten Aussteller und Gäste der Art Basel Paris fanden rauchende Haufen verbrannter Fahrräder und Glasscherben auf den Straßen vor, dazu zahlreiche eingeschlagene Fensterscheiben – nicht nur bei Luxusläden von Dior bis Lacoste auf den Champs-Élysées, sondern auch bei Sneaker-Läden und dem Bäcker nebenan.

Die VIP-Previewtage am Dienstag und Mittwoch verliefen trotzdem sehr erfolgreich. Nach Angaben von Messechef Karim Crippa hatte es zwar einzelne Absagen von Sammlerinnen und Sammlern gegeben, der Besuch der Messe sei insgesamt aber sehr gut gewesen. Bereits am Mittwoch gab es allerdings Gerüchte, dass zumindest die Werke im öffentlichen Raum vor dem Grand Palais aus Angst vor Vandalismus vorzeitig abgebaut werden könnten. Alicja Kwades "L’Élévation des Mondes" beispielsweise, ein rund viereinhalb Meter hoher Turm aus polierten Natursteinkugeln aus aller Welt, wird bereits am Freitag abgebaut, wie die Künstlerin gegenüber Monopol bestätigte – auch wenn die Steinkugeln wirklich nicht leicht kaputtzumachen seien, so Kwade.

Potenzieller Umsatzverlust für Aussteller

In einem internen Schreiben bat die Messe die Aussteller, ihre Präsentationen in den Messekojen im Gebäude bis zum offiziellen Messeschluss am Freitag um 19 Uhr vollständig stehen zu lassen, und kündigte logistische Unterstützung beim vorzeitigen Abbau an.

Für die Aussteller bedeutet der Abbruch einerseits einen potenziellen Umsatzverlust, allerdings findet die große Mehrzahl der Verkäufe ohnehin an den Tagen vor der offiziellen Eröffnung statt. Der Messe selbst werden die Eintrittsgelder der normalerweise sehr gut besuchten Publikumstage fehlen. Und es fehlen zwei Tage Öffnung für die Allgemeinheit. So bleibt die Art Basel Paris diesmal tatsächlich weitgehend den Kunstinsidern vorbehalten – auch das ein trauriger Nebeneffekt.

title_original: Buchtipp: Das grosse Kompendium für digitale Fotografie
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "32 Fotobücher, mehr als 7000 Seiten Fachwissen und das alles für gerade einmal 20 Euro: Der Franzis-Verlag bietet eine umfangreiche digitale Fotobibliothek zum Sonderpreis an. Doch wie wertvoll ist fotografisches Wissen, wenn manche Bücher bereits zehn Jahre alt sind?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Zugegeben, eine etwas ungewöhnliche Buchbesprechung. Persönlich bin ich nach wie vor ein Liebhaber handfester Bücher mit einem möglichst ansprechend gestalteten Cover, die sich – dank Rückenbeschriftung – übersichtlich ins Bücherregal einordnen lassen. Ein Griff, und schon ist man fleissig am Blättern, mit einer Zugriffszeit, die der digitalen Variante weit überlegen ist. Und das alles ohne elektrischen Strom! Wenn man seit Jahrzehnten diese Leseform gewohnt ist, tut man sich mit digitalen Publikationen etwas schwer. Es fehlen die Haptik, das Gefühl, ein richtiges Buch in den Händen zu halten, und vielleicht auch ein wenig die besondere Liebe zum gedruckten Wort."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Dass die digitale Leseform auch ihre Vorzüge hat, ist unbestritten. PDF-Dateien beanspruchen keinen physischen Platz und lassen sich auf geeigneten Geräten überallhin mitnehmen – in der Bahn, im Flugzeug oder in den Urlaub. So kann man problemlos eine ganze Bibliothek mit sich führen. Hinzu kommt die praktische Suchfunktion, mit der sich bestimmte Begriffe oder Themen oft wesentlich schneller finden lassen als in gedruckten Büchern."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bei meiner Vorliebe für gedruckte Bücher ist es also durchaus eine Ausnahme, dass ich Ihnen heute digitalen Lesestoff empfehle. Doch das Angebot des Franzis-Verlags ist derart interessant, dass ich es Ihnen nicht vorenthalten möchte: 32 Fach- und Themenbücher zur Fotografie für insgesamt gerade einmal 20 Euro! Registrieren, bezahlen, herunterladen – fertig."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Allerdings haben die Bücher einen kleinen Schönheitsfehler: Sie sind nicht mehr ganz neuen Datums. Die meisten sind bereits vor einigen Jahren erschienen, und besonders bei technischen Themen sollte man die zwischenzeitliche Entwicklung berücksichtigen. So stammt die «Fotoschule zur digitalen Fotografie» aus dem Jahr 2018 und zeigt naturgemäss nicht mehr die aktuellsten Kameras und Zubehörgeräte. Noch deutlicher wird dies beim Titel «Fotografie mit dem Smartphone» von 2016. Gerade in diesem Bereich haben sich Technik und fotografische Möglichkeiten in den vergangenen zehn Jahren geradezu revolutionär weiterentwickelt."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bei vielen Themen- und Praxisbüchern fällt das Erscheinungsdatum dagegen weniger ins Gewicht. Fotografische Grundlagen, gestalterische Überlegungen und praktische Erfahrungen verlieren nicht so schnell an Gültigkeit wie technische Gerätebeschreibungen. Ob Langzeitbelichtungen, Eulen und Greifvögel oder Schwarzweissfotografie: Wer sich plötzlich für ein bestimmtes Gebiet interessiert und rasch einige fundierte Anregungen und praktische Tipps sucht, wird in dieser Sammlung mit grosser Wahrscheinlichkeit fündig. Dabei sind die Erfahrungen und Empfehlungen spezialisierter Autorinnen und Autoren oft auch dann noch wertvoll, wenn das betreffende Buch schon einige Jahre auf dem Buckel hat."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Und dann ist da natürlich noch der Preis: 20 Euro für mehr als 7000 Seiten Fotowissen. Das entspricht gerade einmal gut 60 Cent pro Buch. Dafür kann man auch die rund 1,2 Gigabyte Speicherplatz auf der Festplatte verschmerzen."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nachstehend stellen wir Ihnen die 32 Buchtitel kurz einzeln vor. Wer mehr über die einzelnen Bücher erfahren möchte, findet weitere Informationen auf der Website des Franzis-Verlags."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Für wen ist diese Büchersammlung? Für alle, die sich für die Fotografie interessieren, ihre Kenntnisse vertiefen oder sich mit neuen fotografischen Themen beschäftigen möchten. Obwohl der Schwerpunkt auf der Digitalfotografie liegt, sind zwei Bücher auch dem Fotografieren auf Film gewidmet. Die Sammlung ist ein reichhaltiger Fundus an Fachwissen, Anregungen und Praxistipps, auf den man immer wieder zurückgreifen kann, wenn man sich über ein bestimmtes Thema informieren möchte. Nicht jedes technische Detail ist noch auf dem neuesten Stand – doch gerade die zeitloseren Grundlagen und praktischen Erfahrungen machen dieses umfangreiche Paket zu einem bemerkenswert preiswerten Nachschlagewerk."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Urs Tillmanns"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.fotointern.ch/wp-uploads/2026/10/Kompendium-Sortiment-1600-1760x1113.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Fotointern"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "32 Bücher über digitale Fotografie als pdf-Dateien"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "photo basics 1. Die Grundlagen der digitalen Fotografie – Christian Haasz In diesem Ratgeber geht es vor allem um die unterschiedlichen Kamerasysteme, die Wahl des richtigen Objektivs, die korrekte Belichtungsmessung, Schärfe und Bildgestaltung."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "photo basics 2. Fotos speichern, bearbeiten und wiederfinden – Ulrich Vermeer, Angela Wulf In diesem Ratgeber geht es vor allem um die Bearbeitung und Verwaltung Ihrer Fotos. Wenn man sich die Mühe macht, gute Bilder zu erstellen, sollten sie nicht im Nirwana verschwinden."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "photo basics 3. Familienfotografie ist mehr als nur eine Passion und birgt einen ganz besonderen Zauber, aber auch besondere Herausforderungen."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Klassische Porträtfotografie – Christian Haasz Effektvoll beleuchtet, modern inszeniert, meisterhaft fotografiert. Was macht ein handwerklich perfektes Porträt aus? Welches Equipment braucht man? Wie stellt man Persönlichkeiten dar?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Langzeitbelichtung – Fotoschule Extra – Charlie Dombrow Langzeitbelichtung ist magisch: Nachziehende Lichtspuren vorbeifahrender Autos, detailreiche Nachtaufnahmen, oder Wasseroberflächen wie aus Samt – all das bedarf einer Langzeitbelichtung."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Fotografie mit dem Smartphone – Simone Naumann, Ulrich Dorn Dieses Buch zeigt alle Facetten der Smartphone-Fotografie: Welche Apps Sie wirklich brauchen, wie Sie Ihre Fotos direkt auf dem Smartphone bearbeiten, wie Sie Bilder machen, die verkaufen"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Fotografie al dente – Jana Mänz, Dr. Susan Brooks-Dammann, Corinna Gissemann Pasta richtig aufs Bild. Foodfotografie – Geniale Bilder, die zum Essen einladen. Lernen Sie die Tricks der Profis mit Step-by-Step-Anleitungen kennen, um selbst Fotos zu machen, die verführen."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bilder die verkaufen – Jana Mänz, Simone Naumann Produkte für Dawanda, Etsy oder ebay verkaufsfördernd fotografieren. Produkte richtig darstellen und dann zum höheren Preis verkaufen. Was braucht es für das perfekte Fotostudio für kleines Geld?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Think Analog – Antonino Zambito Die faszinierende Welt der analogen Fotografie. Alles über Film und Entwicklung."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Coole Bilder mit dem Smartphone – Simone Naumann, Ulrich Dorn Der Fotokurs für Apple, Samsung, Sony und andere. Fotoschule – Regine Heuser Ein wenig Kreativität und eine Handvoll Tipps und Tricks sind die Zutaten für aussergewöhnliche Tierfotos im Zoo – fast so, als hätte man die Tiere in ihrer natürlichen Umgebung fotografiert."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mittelalterfotografie – Charlie Dombrow Fotografische Zeitreise ins Mittelalter. Wo findet man die grandiosen Fotomotive, die uns 500 Jahre zurückversetzen? Die besten Tipps, um Mittelalterfeste und Ritterturniere richtig zu fotografieren."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Vögel fotografieren – Detlef Hase Vögel faszinieren! Oldtimer sind die beste Symbiose von Form, Technik und Faszination."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Fotografie im Garten – Dirk Mann Die Fotoschule für Blumen- und Gartenfreunde. Lassen Sie sich inspirieren mit diesem Ratgeber."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Equi Animo – Die Seele der Pferde – Wiebke Haas Dieser Bildband ist für alle Menschen, die Pferde für das lieben, was sie sind: freie und wunderbar stolze Tiere. Grossformatiger Bildband mit Fotos von über 220, teils preis dotierten Pferden."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Jagdhunde fotografieren – Regine Heuser Hunde vor der Kamera sind kein leichtes Unterfangen und das Fotografieren von Jagdhunden bei der Arbeit ist noch viel schwieriger. article_text:
32 Fotobücher, mehr als 7000 Seiten Fachwissen und das alles für gerade einmal 20 Euro: Der Franzis-Verlag bietet eine umfangreiche digitale Fotobibliothek zum Sonderpreis an. Doch wie wertvoll ist fotografisches Wissen, wenn manche Bücher bereits zehn Jahre alt sind?

Zugegeben, eine etwas ungewöhnliche Buchbesprechung. Persönlich bin ich nach wie vor ein Liebhaber handfester Bücher mit einem möglichst ansprechend gestalteten Cover, die sich – dank Rückenbeschriftung – übersichtlich ins Bücherregal einordnen lassen. Ein Griff, und schon ist man fleissig am Blättern, mit einer Zugriffszeit, die der digitalen Variante weit überlegen ist. Und das alles ohne elektrischen Strom! Wenn man seit Jahrzehnten diese Leseform gewohnt ist, tut man sich mit digitalen Publikationen etwas schwer. Es fehlen die Haptik, das Gefühl, ein richtiges Buch in den Händen zu halten, und vielleicht auch ein wenig die besondere Liebe zum gedruckten Wort.

Dass die digitale Leseform auch ihre Vorzüge hat, ist unbestritten. PDF-Dateien beanspruchen keinen physischen Platz und lassen sich auf geeigneten Geräten überallhin mitnehmen – in der Bahn, im Flugzeug oder in den Urlaub. So kann man problemlos eine ganze Bibliothek mit sich führen. Hinzu kommt die praktische Suchfunktion, mit der sich bestimmte Begriffe oder Themen oft wesentlich schneller finden lassen als in gedruckten Büchern.

Bei meiner Vorliebe für gedruckte Bücher ist es also durchaus eine Ausnahme, dass ich Ihnen heute digitalen Lesestoff empfehle. Doch das Angebot des Franzis-Verlags ist derart interessant, dass ich es Ihnen nicht vorenthalten möchte: 32 Fach- und Themenbücher zur Fotografie für insgesamt gerade einmal 20 Euro! Registrieren, bezahlen, herunterladen – fertig.

Allerdings haben die Bücher einen kleinen Schönheitsfehler: Sie sind nicht mehr ganz neuen Datums. Die meisten sind bereits vor einigen Jahren erschienen, und besonders bei technischen Themen sollte man die zwischenzeitliche Entwicklung berücksichtigen. So stammt die «Fotoschule zur digitalen Fotografie» aus dem Jahr 2018 und zeigt naturgemäss nicht mehr die aktuellsten Kameras und Zubehörgeräte. Noch deutlicher wird dies beim Titel «Fotografie mit dem Smartphone» von 2016. Gerade in diesem Bereich haben sich Technik und fotografische Möglichkeiten in den vergangenen zehn Jahren geradezu revolutionär weiterentwickelt.

Bei vielen Themen- und Praxisbüchern fällt das Erscheinungsdatum dagegen weniger ins Gewicht. Fotografische Grundlagen, gestalterische Überlegungen und praktische Erfahrungen verlieren nicht so schnell an Gültigkeit wie technische Gerätebeschreibungen. Ob Langzeitbelichtungen, Eulen und Greifvögel oder Schwarzweissfotografie: Wer sich plötzlich für ein bestimmtes Gebiet interessiert und rasch einige fundierte Anregungen und praktische Tipps sucht, wird in dieser Sammlung mit grosser Wahrscheinlichkeit fündig. Dabei sind die Erfahrungen und Empfehlungen spezialisierter Autorinnen und Autoren oft auch dann noch wertvoll, wenn das betreffende Buch schon einige Jahre auf dem Buckel hat.

Und dann ist da natürlich noch der Preis: 20 Euro für mehr als 7000 Seiten Fotowissen. Das entspricht gerade einmal gut 60 Cent pro Buch. Dafür kann man auch die rund 1,2 Gigabyte Speicherplatz auf der Festplatte verschmerzen.

Nachstehend stellen wir Ihnen die 32 Buchtitel kurz einzeln vor. Wer mehr über die einzelnen Bücher erfahren möchte, findet weitere Informationen auf der Website des Franzis-Verlags.

Für wen ist diese Büchersammlung? Für alle, die sich für die Fotografie interessieren, ihre Kenntnisse vertiefen oder sich mit neuen fotografischen Themen beschäftigen möchten. Obwohl der Schwerpunkt auf der Digitalfotografie liegt, sind zwei Bücher auch dem Fotografieren auf Film gewidmet. Die Sammlung ist ein reichhaltiger Fundus an Fachwissen, Anregungen und Praxistipps, auf den man immer wieder zurückgreifen kann, wenn man sich über ein bestimmtes Thema informieren möchte. Nicht jedes technische Detail ist noch auf dem neuesten Stand – doch gerade die zeitloseren Grundlagen und praktischen Erfahrungen machen dieses umfangreiche Paket zu einem bemerkenswert preiswerten Nachschlagewerk.

Urs Tillmanns

32 Bücher über digitale Fotografie als pdf-Dateien

photo basics 1. Die Grundlagen der digitalen Fotografie – Christian Haasz In diesem Ratgeber geht es vor allem um die unterschiedlichen Kamerasysteme, die Wahl des richtigen Objektivs, die korrekte Belichtungsmessung, Schärfe und Bildgestaltung.

photo basics 2. Fotos speichern, bearbeiten und wiederfinden – Ulrich Vermeer, Angela Wulf In diesem Ratgeber geht es vor allem um die Bearbeitung und Verwaltung Ihrer Fotos. Wenn man sich die Mühe macht, gute Bilder zu erstellen, sollten sie nicht im Nirwana verschwinden.

photo basics 3. Fotos zeigen, die begeistern – Ulrich Vermeer, Angela Wulf In diesem Ratgeber geht es vor allem um die Vor- und Nachteile der unterschiedlichen Plattformen im Netz und um das Fotobuch: Design, Typografie und der Bildformate.

Familienbande – Simone Naumann Alles, was ambitionierte Familien-Paparazzi wissen müssen. Familienfotografie ist mehr als nur eine Passion und birgt einen ganz besonderen Zauber, aber auch besondere Herausforderungen.

Klassische Porträtfotografie – Christian Haasz Effektvoll beleuchtet, modern inszeniert, meisterhaft fotografiert. Was macht ein handwerklich perfektes Porträt aus? Welches Equipment braucht man? Wie stellt man Persönlichkeiten dar?

Langzeitbelichtung – Fotoschule Extra – Charlie Dombrow Langzeitbelichtung ist magisch: Nachziehende Lichtspuren vorbeifahrender Autos, detailreiche Nachtaufnahmen, oder Wasseroberflächen wie aus Samt – all das bedarf einer Langzeitbelichtung.

Fotografie mit dem Smartphone – Simone Naumann, Ulrich Dorn Dieses Buch zeigt alle Facetten der Smartphone-Fotografie: Welche Apps Sie wirklich brauchen, wie Sie Ihre Fotos direkt auf dem Smartphone bearbeiten, wie Sie Bilder machen, die verkaufen

Fotografie al dente – Jana Mänz, Dr. Susan Brooks-Dammann, Corinna Gissemann Pasta richtig aufs Bild. Foodfotografie – Geniale Bilder, die zum Essen einladen. Lernen Sie die Tricks der Profis mit Step-by-Step-Anleitungen kennen, um selbst Fotos zu machen, die verführen.

Bilder die verkaufen – Jana Mänz, Simone Naumann Produkte für Dawanda, Etsy oder ebay verkaufsfördernd fotografieren. Produkte richtig darstellen und dann zum höheren Preis verkaufen. Was braucht es für das perfekte Fotostudio für kleines Geld?

Think Analog – Antonino Zambito Die faszinierende Welt der analogen Fotografie. Die analoge Fotografie als weitere Facette sehen. Was gibt es heute noch an Apparaten, Zubehör und Filmmaterial? Alles über Film und Entwicklung.

Coole Bilder mit dem Smartphone – Simone Naumann, Ulrich Dorn Der Fotokurs für Apple, Samsung, Sony und andere. Das Smartphone hat man heute immer dabei und alle machen auf Anhieb gute Bilder. Für noch bessere Bilder, ein paar wichtige Dinge beachten.

Nackt! – Das Profibuch der Aktfotografie – Stefan Weis Erotik kunstvoll fotografieren. Mit der richtigen Vorbereitung, dem nötigen Feingefühl und dem Wissen von Profifotografen, wird aus der Knipserei, echte, stimmungsvolle Körperfotografie.

ZOO! Fotoschule – Regine Heuser Ein wenig Kreativität und eine Handvoll Tipps und Tricks sind die Zutaten für aussergewöhnliche Tierfotos im Zoo – fast so, als hätte man die Tiere in ihrer natürlichen Umgebung fotografiert.

Mittelalterfotografie – Charlie Dombrow Fotografische Zeitreise ins Mittelalter. Wo findet man die grandiosen Fotomotive, die uns 500 Jahre zurückversetzen? Die besten Tipps, um Mittelalterfeste und Ritterturniere richtig zu fotografieren.

Vögel fotografieren – Detlef Hase Vögel faszinieren! An den guten Vogelbeobachtungs­plätzen steigt die Zahl der Vogelbeobachter stetig. Viele haben den Wunsch, das Beobachtete als Bild mit nach Hause zu nehmen.

Oldtimer & Youngtimer fotografieren – Charlie Dombrow Autos und Motorräder richtig in Szene setzen. Richtig schöne Autos sollten richtig schön fotografiert werden. Oldtimer sind die beste Symbiose von Form, Technik und Faszination.

Fotografie im Garten – Dirk Mann Die Fotoschule für Blumen- und Gartenfreunde. Ein Garten verändert sich ständig, denn sein Inhalt lebt und wandelt sich und somit auch die Motive. Lassen Sie sich inspirieren mit diesem Ratgeber.

Equi Animo – Die Seele der Pferde – Wiebke Haas Dieser Bildband ist für alle Menschen, die Pferde für das lieben, was sie sind: freie und wunderbar stolze Tiere. Grossformatiger Bildband mit Fotos von über 220, teils preis dotierten Pferden.

Jagdhunde fotografieren – Regine Heuser Hunde vor der Kamera sind kein leichtes Unterfangen und das Fotografieren von Jagdhunden bei der Arbeit ist noch viel schwieriger. Fangen Sie die Dynamik und Lebensfreude in besten Bildern ein.

Fotografie Lost Places – Charlie Dombrow Das Fotohandbuch für Urbexer. Orte mit Geschichte. Orte mit Geheimnissen. Verwunschene, verborgene, verfallene, manchmal schon vergessene Orte. Bilder mit Geschichte, die faszinieren.

Fototouren an geheimen Orten – Charlie Dombrow; Andreas Böttger; Thilo Wiebers Verlassen – Vergessen – Verboten: Die Lost places Fotografie und alles was man dazu wissen muss. Motive finden, die nicht jeder kennt, und immer die richtige Ausrüstung dabei haben.

Das Blitzbuch – Michael Nagel In diesem Buch lernen Sie, Begriffe und Funktionen der Blitztechnik praktisch einzusetzen. Was ist entfesseltes Blitzen, wie holt man die richtige Stimmung ins Bild und wie malt man mit Licht?

Coole Bilder mit der Sofortbildkamera – Antonino Zambito Das besondere Erlebnis einer Sofortbildkamera. Umgang, Möglichkeiten und der besondere Bildlook. Dabei ist jedes Bild ein Unikat. Die besten Tipps für noch bessere sofortige Erinnerungen.

Meine Katze – Regine Heuser Stellen Sie sich der Herausforderung und fangen Sie die Dynamik und Lebensfreude Ihrer Katze in wirkungsvollen Bildern ein. Wie entstehen gefühlsbetonte Katzenbilder mit Aussage und Charme?

Eulen & Greifvögel fotografieren – Tanja Brandt Dieses Buch steht für die Schönheit der Eulen und Greifvögel. Wo und wie findet man diese scheuen Vögel, wann ist die beste Tageszeit und wie bekommt man faszinierende Bilder im Flug?

Tierfotografie – Fotoschule Extra – Wiebke Haas Der treue Blick, die kalte Schnauze, Euphorie, Schwanzwedeln. Hunde sind einfach klasse, auch Katzen und Pferde haben richtig gute Porträts verdient. Wichtige Tipps in dieser Fotoschule Extra.

Foto-Drohnen – Uwe Schneider Das Handbuch für den Copter-Piloten. Neue Perspektiven und Herausforderungen für jeden Fotografen. Alles über die Technik der Drohnen, mit viel Foto- und Video-Know-how.

Makrofotografie – Andreas Kolossa Welche Objektive braucht der engagierte Makrofotograf? Wie kann man Schärfe und Belichtung seinen Gestaltungsabsichten entsprechend steuern? Wie entstehen Bilder mit bezauberndem Bokeh?

Richtig blitzen – Fotoschule Extra – Michael Nagel Das Fotografieren mit einer künstlichen Lichtquelle ist das selbstverständliche Mittel bei wenig Licht. Wie setzt man den Blitz kreativ ein und welche Lichtformer für spezielle Lichteffekte gibt es?

Schwarz-Weiss-Fotografie – Antonino Zambito, Andreas Pflaum Fotografieren in Schwarz-Weiss ist mehr als nur das Weglassen von Farbe. Durch die Reduktion des Bunten auf Graustufen entsteht eine Konzentration auf Formen und Hell-Dunkel-Übergänge.

99 Foto-Hacks – Christian Haas Das sind die 99 coolsten Foto-Hacks. Lassen Sie sich inspirieren und zeigen Sie der Welt, wie man sie noch interessanter fotografieren kann. Hier findet man schnelle Hilfe, wenn man nicht weiter weiss.

Fotoschule – Das neue Handbuch – Ulrich Vermeer, Christian Haasz, Angela Wulf Die richtige Kamera und Ausrüstung finden, Kameratechnik verstehen, Bildgestaltung und Bildbearbeitung beherrschen und die fertigen Fotos veröffentlichen. Das Wissen dazu gibt es hier.

Die Autorinnen und Autoren

Charlie Dombrow fotografiert bevorzugt Akt, Architektur, Bäume, Landschaften, Mittelalter und Ruinen aller Art. Seit 1996 fotografiert er Backplates für Bildmontagen und erstellt realistische Composings mit Menschen und Autos.

Christian Haasz arbeitete nach dem Studium bis 1999 als Redakteur, Chef vom Dienst und stellvertretender Chefredakteur für ein Computermagazin. Seit 1999 ist er selbstständiger Medienschaffender. Er ist Autor mehrerer erfolgreicher Fachbücher.

Wiebke Haasz ist mit Tieren aufgewachsen und wurde nach ihrem Abitur staatlich geprüfte Berufsfotografin. Seitdem arbeitet sie als Tierfotografin in der ganzen Welt. Ihre Bilder erscheinen in Zeitschriften und Magazinen und sind Thema einiger TV-Produktionen.

Andreas Karpe Gora ist gefragter Sportfotograf und Bildjournalist für die Tagespresse und Entertainment. Er arbeitet als Bildredakteur bei der Bildagentur Sport Moments, bietet Kurse zum Erlernen der Sportfotografie an und publiziert Fachbücher.

Andreas Kolossa begann im Alter von 25 Jahren mit der Natur- und insbesondere der Makrofotografie von Schmetterlingen. Mit seinen Fotos möchte er die Zauberwelt der Natur wieder in den Fokus bringen. Er ist ehrenamtlich im Naturschutz.

Simone Naumann arbeitet seit 2009 freiberuflich als gefragte Spezialistin für Produktfotografie. Ihr Schwerpunkt liegt im Lichtdesign. Sie studierte an der Fotoacademie Amsterdam, und der Prager Fotoschule Österreich und bildete sich mit namhaften Fotografen fort.

Uwe Schneider ist seit mehr als 35 Jahren als Journalist in verschiedenen Positionen bei Agenturen, Printmedien und auf selbstständiger Basis tätig. Früher analoger Fotograf mit eigenem Entwicklungslabor, wurde er ein Wegbereiter für die digitale Fotografie.

Ulrich Vermeer , der Spezialist für Kameratechnik, Datenablage, Datenaustausch und den sinnvollen Einsatz einer Cloud, damit alle Bilder auf dem PC, Apple, Smartphone oder Tablet betrachtet werden können.

Angela Wulf ist Expertin für Bildbearbeitung und das Präsentieren von Fotos. Neben den Essentials der Bildbearbeitung mit Adobe Photoshop Elements zeigt sie, wie man mit Fotobüchern quasi zum eigenen Verleger wird oder zu Hause seine eigene Galerie schafft.

Antonino Zambito hatte lange Auslandsaufenthalte, die seine Art zu fotografieren stark beeinflusst haben. Er arbeitete als Pressefotograf und begann 2005, eigene Ausstellungen zu machen und Fotokurse zu geben. Er konzipierte dabei eine eigene Lehrmethode.

Bibliografie

32 umfassende Fotografie-Ratgeber in einer einzigartigen PDF-Sammlung – und dies zu einem unschlagbaren Paket-Preis. Das Kompendium ist ohne Limitierung und Zeitbeschränkung als echten Download erhältlich und auf PC, Mac, Tablet oder Smartphone einsetzbar.

title_original: Cultura nei piccoli comuni: il bando del MIC finanzia 27 progetti in tutta Italia

La graduatoria assegna complessivamente 1.445.100 euro a interventi che coinvolgeranno 40 Comuni italiani. Sono state 1.060 le candidature presentate da amministrazioni provenienti da tutto il territorio nazionale", "links": [{"text": "Cultura nei piccoli comuni", "url": "https://creativitacontemporanea.cultura.gov.it/cultura-piccolicomuni-edizione1/"}, {"text": "DGCC – Direzione Generale Creatività Contemporanea", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/tag/dgcc-direzione-generale-creativita-contemporanea/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Oltre mille candidature da tutta Italia"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "L’iniziativa, lanciata lo scorso giugno e rivolta ai centri con meno di 25mila abitanti, è promossa nell’ambito del Dipartimento per le Attività Culturali del MiC, con l’Unità di missione per la cooperazione culturale con l’Africa e il Mediterraneo allargato e il Piano Olivetti per la Cultura, con il supporto amministrativo di ALES. L’avviso punta a sostenere progettualità capaci di mettere in relazione patrimonio culturale, produzione contemporanea e partecipazione delle comunità, favorendo allo stesso tempo collaborazioni tra enti pubblici, realtà del Terzo settore, associazioni e soggetti attivi sui territori."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/castrignano-de-greci-1757360255563.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "Castrignano de Greci", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La Commissione di valutazione ha selezionato i progetti considerando, tra gli altri criteri, la qualità delle proposte, la capacità di costruire partenariati e la sostenibilità delle attività nel medio e lungo periodo. I 27 beneficiari, tra Comuni singoli e capofila di reti che coinvolgono complessivamente 40 amministrazioni, sono Bagaladi (RC), Seui (OG), Caccamo (PA), San Giorgio Albanese (CS), Mongiana (VV), Fabbriche di Vergemoli (LU), Campoli Appennino (FR), Curti (CE), Prepotto (UD), Capua (CE), Costanzana (VC), Flumeri (AV), Orani (NU), San Giovanni a Piro (SA), Amelia (TR), Amendolara (CS), Borgorose (RI), Capoterra (CA), Castrignano de’ Greci (LE), Montemurro (PZ), Sarsina (FC), Sedilo (OR), Sustinente (MN), Trebisacce (CS), Canale Monterano (RM), Ploaghe (SS) e Sala Consilina (SA)."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Dal patrimonio alla rigenerazione urbana"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Gli interventi selezionati attraversano ambiti differenti, dalla tutela e valorizzazione del patrimonio materiale e immateriale alla rigenerazione urbana e territoriale, fino alla produzione culturale contemporanea. Una parte dei progetti riguarda inoltre il miglioramento dell’accessibilità e della fruizione culturale, mentre altri prevedono l’utilizzo delle tecnologie digitali come strumenti per ampliare conoscenza, partecipazione e inclusione."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Panorama_trebisacce.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Trebisacce", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Alla base della misura c’è il riconoscimento dei piccoli centri come luoghi nei quali il patrimonio culturale può diventare uno strumento per consolidare reti territoriali e sviluppare nuove forme di collaborazione tra istituzioni e comunità. L’obiettivo dichiarato è favorire interventi capaci di produrre effetti anche oltre la durata del finanziamento."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Cultura nei piccoli comuni: la seconda edizione entro il 2026"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Con la pubblicazione della graduatoria prende ora avvio la fase attuativa dei 27 progetti finanziati. article_text:
Sono 27 i Comuni beneficiari della prima edizione di Cultura nei piccoli comuni , l’avviso pubblico promosso dalla DGCC – Direzione Generale Creatività Contemporanea del Ministero della Cultura per sostenere progetti di valorizzazione culturale e rafforzamento delle comunità locali. La graduatoria assegna complessivamente 1.445.100 euro a interventi che coinvolgeranno 40 Comuni italiani. Sono state 1.060 le candidature presentate da amministrazioni provenienti da tutto il territorio nazionale

Oltre mille candidature da tutta Italia

L’iniziativa, lanciata lo scorso giugno e rivolta ai centri con meno di 25mila abitanti, è promossa nell’ambito del Dipartimento per le Attività Culturali del MiC, con l’Unità di missione per la cooperazione culturale con l’Africa e il Mediterraneo allargato e il Piano Olivetti per la Cultura, con il supporto amministrativo di ALES. L’avviso punta a sostenere progettualità capaci di mettere in relazione patrimonio culturale, produzione contemporanea e partecipazione delle comunità, favorendo allo stesso tempo collaborazioni tra enti pubblici, realtà del Terzo settore, associazioni e soggetti attivi sui territori.

La Commissione di valutazione ha selezionato i progetti considerando, tra gli altri criteri, la qualità delle proposte, la capacità di costruire partenariati e la sostenibilità delle attività nel medio e lungo periodo. I 27 beneficiari, tra Comuni singoli e capofila di reti che coinvolgono complessivamente 40 amministrazioni, sono Bagaladi (RC), Seui (OG), Caccamo (PA), San Giorgio Albanese (CS), Mongiana (VV), Fabbriche di Vergemoli (LU), Campoli Appennino (FR), Curti (CE), Prepotto (UD), Capua (CE), Costanzana (VC), Flumeri (AV), Orani (NU), San Giovanni a Piro (SA), Amelia (TR), Amendolara (CS), Borgorose (RI), Capoterra (CA), Castrignano de’ Greci (LE), Montemurro (PZ), Sarsina (FC), Sedilo (OR), Sustinente (MN), Trebisacce (CS), Canale Monterano (RM), Ploaghe (SS) e Sala Consilina (SA).

Dal patrimonio alla rigenerazione urbana

Gli interventi selezionati attraversano ambiti differenti, dalla tutela e valorizzazione del patrimonio materiale e immateriale alla rigenerazione urbana e territoriale, fino alla produzione culturale contemporanea. Una parte dei progetti riguarda inoltre il miglioramento dell’accessibilità e della fruizione culturale, mentre altri prevedono l’utilizzo delle tecnologie digitali come strumenti per ampliare conoscenza, partecipazione e inclusione.

Alla base della misura c’è il riconoscimento dei piccoli centri come luoghi nei quali il patrimonio culturale può diventare uno strumento per consolidare reti territoriali e sviluppare nuove forme di collaborazione tra istituzioni e comunità. L’obiettivo dichiarato è favorire interventi capaci di produrre effetti anche oltre la durata del finanziamento.

Cultura nei piccoli comuni: la seconda edizione entro il 2026

Con la pubblicazione della graduatoria prende ora avvio la fase attuativa dei 27 progetti finanziati. L’iniziativa è destinata inoltre a proseguire: entro la fine del 2026 è prevista la pubblicazione della seconda edizione di Cultura nei piccoli comuni , dedicata al sostegno di attività da realizzare durante l’estate 2027.

title_original: Jordan Rossi: “Joy Is Political in Its Own Way”
editorial_title_zh: 乔丹·罗西：“快乐本身就带有政治意味”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 在米兰时装周期间展出的《归乡》（Homecoming）中，英国摄影师兼电影制作人乔丹·罗西在时尚摄影、纯艺术肖像与社会反思的交汇点上探讨了身份、男性气质与酷儿文化。 L’article Jordan Rossi: “Joy Is Political in Its…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔丹·罗西（Jordan Rossi）一直在微妙的边缘行走。他拥有英国、意大利和爱尔兰血统，拍摄伦敦酷儿现场和奢侈品牌广告时同样坚定，从不显得背叛其中任何一方。他的目光将生动、常常不羁的时尚摄影转化为私密与社会肖像的工具。他只有一个执念：捕捉拍摄对象卸下防备的瞬间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你的首个展览题为《归乡》（Homecoming），既诉说着回归，也诉说着归属感。这个词对你意味着什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔丹·罗西：《归乡》感觉是唯一可能的标题。我在意大利和爱尔兰这两种文化之间长大，但我出生在伦敦并在那里长大——所以我对“家”这个概念一直有着有些复杂的感情。我想我从来没有完全觉得自己属于某一种单一的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "将这组作品带到意大利感觉就像画上了一个圆满的句号。这些照片涵盖了我近十年的生活，创作于伦敦、洛杉矶及其他地方。把它们带到这里——一个构成我身份和家庭一部分的国家，感觉非常个人化。但随着时间的推移，“家”对我来说已经不再那么具有地理意义。它是你身边的人、你找到的社群，以及最终你为自己创造的空间。从这个意义上说，《归乡》既关乎我现在在哪里，也关乎我来自哪里。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/lukita-maxwell-804x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "卢基塔·麦克斯韦（Lukita Maxwell）© 乔丹·罗西，图片由艺术家及鲁宾画廊（Galleria Rubin）提供", "credit": "Blind Magazine", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你既拍摄过伦敦东部的酷儿社群，也拍摄过劳斯莱斯（Rolls-Royce）的广告。这两个世界难道不冲突吗？你是如何在它们之间游走的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔丹·罗西：我从来不觉得它们之间存在冲突。规模、预算和期望可能完全不同，但归根结底，我感兴趣的东西依然是一样的：人、个性，以及围绕他们构建一个世界。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我同样认为，酷儿艺术家不应该仅仅局限在酷儿空间里生存。我可以拍摄伦敦东部一家俱乐部里的人，然后去执导一个全球品牌的广告——这两者依然都可以包含我的观点。如果说有什么不同的话，在这些世界之间穿梭对我而言很重要。塑造了我的经历和社群不可避免地会融入商业作品中，而商业世界的资源也会反哺我的个人创作。我不希望我职业生涯的任何一面与另一面完全隔绝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "人们通常将你的摄影描述为酷儿的、具有社会责任感的、扎根于时尚与肖像的。关于你的作品以及它带你去过的地方，你还会补充些什么？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔丹·罗西：我可能会补充说，其中贯穿着一种表演感。我对我们为了镜头而构建的自我版本很感兴趣：时尚、性取向、男性气质、女性气质、名气与魅力。肖像摄影可以记录一个人，但它也可以允许他们在某一刻变成别的东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在过去的十年里，这把我带入了截然不同的环境中——从新兴表演者和酷儿社群成员到演员、音乐人、时装屋和全球品牌。我拍摄了一些早在自己职业拿起相机之前就十分崇拜的人，这至今仍让人觉得有些超现实。但现在当我审视这些作品时，吸引我的不一定是对方是否出名。而是贯穿所有作品的那种同样的求知欲。我会被那些对自我有着强烈认知的人——或者正在探索自我的人所吸引。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔丹·罗西：随着时间的推移，我意识到每当我增加一个新的专业领域，它就会改变我对待其他一切事物的方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有一些直觉和技能在它们之间是相通的。摄影让我更加意识到你与镜头前的人之间建立的关系。它可以是极其私密的——仅仅是两个人试图一起去寻找某种东西。学会如何建立这种信任，改变了我重回导演工作时与表演者合作的方式。同样，多年来的电影制作和创意总监经历也让我对静态图像有了不同的思考。我很少只去想某个画面是否美丽；我在思考它周围的世界、角色、情感，以及这个图像试图表达什么。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这归根结底就是我如何将这三者结合在一起：它们已经成为同一种视觉语言的一部分。我经常在不知不觉中，将从一个领域学到的东西带到另一个领域。现在我不再那么在意某个身份究竟让我成为摄影师、导演还是创意总监——我更关心的是如何找到最佳方式来讲述眼前这个故事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在你的作品中，你选择展现 LGBTQIA+ 社群的快乐，而不是他们的创伤。你是否对这个社群感到一种特殊的责任感——如果是的话，它是什么样子的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "乔丹·罗西：当然——尽管我尽量不让这种责任感变成这样一种观念：即认为存在着一种正确的方式来代表像我们这样庞大且多元的社群。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在很长一段时间里，许多 LGBTQIA+ 的故事都是通过悲剧、排斥或苦难来建构的。这些故事真实且重要，但它们并不代表酷儿生活的全部。我变得对拍摄它的另一面更感兴趣：友谊、性、幽默、美、荒诞、自信、亲密和快乐。这并不是为了否认艰难的事物，而是因为这些事物本身也具有政治意义。看到酷儿群体尽情享受美好时光、占据空间、被人渴望而不是为自己的存在而道歉，这其中蕴含着力量。", "translated": true}, {"type": article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Jordan Rossi has always walked a fine line. British with Italian and Irish roots, he shoots the London queer scene and luxury brand campaigns with equal conviction, never appearing to betray either. His gaze turns fashion photography — vivid, often irreverent — into a tool for intimate and social portraiture. With a single obsession: catching the moment his subjects drop the mask."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The title of your first exhibition, “Homecoming”, speaks of both return and belonging. What does that word mean to you?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Jordan Rossi : “Homecoming” felt like the only possible title. I grew up between two cultures, Italian and Irish, but I was born and raised in London — so I’ve always had a slightly complicated relationship with the idea of “home”. I don’t think I’ve ever felt entirely one thing or another."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bringing this body of work to Italy feels like closing a circle. These photographs cover nearly a decade of my life, made in London, Los Angeles and elsewhere. Bringing them here, to a country that is part of my identity and my family, feels very personal. But with time, “home” has become less geographical for me. It’s the people you surround yourself with, the communities you find, and eventually the space you create for yourself. In that sense, “Homecoming” is as much about where I am now as it is about where I came from."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.blind-magazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/lukita-maxwell-804x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Lukita Maxwell © Jordan Rossi, courtesy of the artist and Galleria Rubin", "credit": "Blind Magazine"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "You have shot the queer community of East London just as much as campaigns for Rolls-Royce. Are these two worlds not in conflict, and how do you move between them?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Jordan Rossi : I’ve never really seen them as being in conflict. The scale, budgets and expectations might be completely different, but ultimately I’m still interested in the same things: people, character, and creating a world around them."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "I also don’t think queer artists should have to exist solely within queer spaces. I can photograph someone in a club in East London and then direct a campaign for a global brand — both can still contain my point of view. If anything, moving between those worlds matters to me. The experiences and communities that shaped me inevitably find their way into the commercial work, and the resources of the commercial world feed back into my personal work. I don’t want either side of my career to exist in isolation from the other."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Your photography is generally described as queer, committed, rooted in fashion and portraiture. What would you add about your work and where it has taken you?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Jordan Rossi : I’d probably add that there’s a sense of performance running through a lot of it. I’m interested in the version of ourselves that we construct for the camera: fashion, sexuality, masculinity, femininity, celebrity, glamour. Portraiture can document somebody, but it can also give them permission to become something else for a moment."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Over the past decade that has taken me into very different rooms — from emerging performers and people within the queer community to actors, musicians, fashion houses and global brands. article_text:
Jordan Rossi has always walked a fine line. British with Italian and Irish roots, he shoots the London queer scene and luxury brand campaigns with equal conviction, never appearing to betray either. His gaze turns fashion photography — vivid, often irreverent — into a tool for intimate and social portraiture. With a single obsession: catching the moment his subjects drop the mask.

The title of your first exhibition, “Homecoming”, speaks of both return and belonging. What does that word mean to you?

Jordan Rossi : “Homecoming” felt like the only possible title. I grew up between two cultures, Italian and Irish, but I was born and raised in London — so I’ve always had a slightly complicated relationship with the idea of “home”. I don’t think I’ve ever felt entirely one thing or another.

Bringing this body of work to Italy feels like closing a circle. These photographs cover nearly a decade of my life, made in London, Los Angeles and elsewhere. Bringing them here, to a country that is part of my identity and my family, feels very personal. But with time, “home” has become less geographical for me. It’s the people you surround yourself with, the communities you find, and eventually the space you create for yourself. In that sense, “Homecoming” is as much about where I am now as it is about where I came from.

You have shot the queer community of East London just as much as campaigns for Rolls-Royce. Are these two worlds not in conflict, and how do you move between them?

Jordan Rossi : I’ve never really seen them as being in conflict. The scale, budgets and expectations might be completely different, but ultimately I’m still interested in the same things: people, character, and creating a world around them.

I also don’t think queer artists should have to exist solely within queer spaces. I can photograph someone in a club in East London and then direct a campaign for a global brand — both can still contain my point of view. If anything, moving between those worlds matters to me. The experiences and communities that shaped me inevitably find their way into the commercial work, and the resources of the commercial world feed back into my personal work. I don’t want either side of my career to exist in isolation from the other.

Your photography is generally described as queer, committed, rooted in fashion and portraiture. What would you add about your work and where it has taken you?

Jordan Rossi : I’d probably add that there’s a sense of performance running through a lot of it. I’m interested in the version of ourselves that we construct for the camera: fashion, sexuality, masculinity, femininity, celebrity, glamour. Portraiture can document somebody, but it can also give them permission to become something else for a moment.

Over the past decade that has taken me into very different rooms — from emerging performers and people within the queer community to actors, musicians, fashion houses and global brands. I’ve photographed people I admired long before I ever picked up a camera professionally, which still feels slightly surreal. But when I look across the work now, what interests me isn’t necessarily who is famous and who isn’t. It’s that the same curiosity runs through all of it. I’m drawn to people who have a strong sense of who they are — or who are in the process of discovering it.

You are a photographer, a filmmaker and a creative director all at once. Concretely, how do you hold those three roles together?

Jordan Rossi : What I’ve realised over time is that every time I’ve added another discipline, it has changed the way I approach everything else.

There are instincts and skills that move between them. Photography made me much more aware of the relationship you build with the person in front of your camera. It can be incredibly intimate — just two people trying to find something together. Learning how to create that trust changed the way I worked with performers when I returned to directing. In the same way, years of filmmaking and creative direction have made me think differently about still images. I’m rarely just thinking about whether something looks beautiful; I’m thinking about the world around it, the character, the emotion, and what the image is trying to say.

That’s ultimately how I hold all three together: they’ve become part of the same visual language. I’m constantly taking things I’ve learned in one area into another, often without consciously realizing it. I’m less interested now in whether something makes me a photographer, director or creative director — and more interested in finding the best way to tell the story in front of me.

In your work, you have chosen to show the joy of the LGBTQIA+ community rather than its trauma. Do you feel a particular responsibility towards that community — and if so, what does it look like?

Jordan Rossi : Absolutely — although I try not to let that responsibility turn into the idea that there is one correct way to represent a community as enormous and varied as ours.

For a long time, so many LGBTQIA+ stories were framed through tragedy, rejection or suffering. Those stories are real and important, but they aren’t the entirety of queer life. I became much more interested in photographing the other side of it: friendship, sex, humor, beauty, ridiculousness, confidence, intimacy and joy. Not as a denial of the difficult things, but because those things are also political in their own way. There is power in seeing queer people simply having a brilliant time, taking up space, being desired rather than apologising for being there.

My responsibility is really to the people in front of my camera. I want them to feel they have agency in how they’re represented, and I want the work to come from being part of a community rather than looking at it from the outside. I don’t think my job is to speak for LGBTQIA+ people. It’s to contribute my perspective to a much bigger, messier and more interesting story.

Jordan Rossi’s show “Homecoming” is on view at Galleria Rubin , Milan (Italy), from September 22 to October 3rd, 2026.

article_text:
Constantin Film and Sony Pictures’ horror reboot “ Resident Evil ” secured the top spot at the mainland China box office for the third consecutive weekend, grossing RMB37.6 million ($5.6 million) over the Oct. 23–25 frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway.

Since rolling out during the Golden Week holiday corridor on Oct. 5, the film has generated a cumulative haul of $64.8 million.

Related Stories

Fox Commits to Carrying Non-Fox Content on Roku for at Least 3 Years as DOJ Closes Antitrust Investigation

Fox and Endemol Shine Team to Adapt 'Fear Factor' as a Scripted Microdrama Series for My Drama App

New Classics Pictures’ crime procedural drama “ Traces of Justice ” held onto second position, taking in $4.7 million in its fourth weekend. Directed by Chen Sicheng (“Detective Chinatown”) and co-written with Zhang Ji and Yan Zijie, the period investigation epic has lifted its cumulative cume to $92.4 million since premiering on Oct. 1. Starring Zhang Yi, Ma Li, and Chen Minghao alongside guest appearances by Karry Wang, Fan Chengcheng, and Chen Feiyu, the multi-decade drama chronicles an elite public security detective unravelling major criminal mysteries based on real cases.

Beijing Joy Fun Pictures’ domestic body-swap comedy “Mr. & Mrs. Pardon” remained in third place, generating $2.6 million over the three-day weekend to lift its cumulative gross to $55.5 million. Directed by Shen Chunyang and written by Ma Duo, the satirical feature stars real-life comedic pair Shen Chunyang and Xiao Shenyang alongside Jia Bing and Yu Yang as an uninspired middle-aged couple forced to navigate marriage and domestic friction after swapping bodies.

Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “ Once Upon a Time in the Middle East ” took fourth position in its eleventh weekend of release, collecting $800,000. Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) and starring Shen Teng, Jiang Qiming, Aarif Rahman, and Omar Sherif, the enduring summer blockbuster has amassed a cumulative total of $355.5 million since launching on Aug. 11.

Pearl Studio’s computer-animated fantasy comedy “ All Wishes Come True! ” rounded out the top five, pulling in $600,000 over its two-day weekend frame. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the long-running family hit has reached a cumulative total of $306.6 million across 15 weeks in release since opening on July 18.

Mainland China’s overall weekend box office dropped to a muted $18.6 million, reflecting a pronounced post-holiday slump across the theatrical landscape. The 2026 year-to-date box office reached $4.7 billion, trailing the same period in 2025 by 29.1%.

article_text:
Issue

New Currents: Ann Zhao

ANN ZHAO ’s

Untitled , 2011, acrylic on canvas board, 41 × 61 × 3.5 cm (left); and

Curse , 2026, acrylic on canvas, 150 × 200 × 4 cm (right); at “Spillover,” Empty Gallery, Hong Kong, 2026. Courtesy the artist and Empty Gallery.

For her solo exhibition “Spillover” (2026) at Hong Kong’s Empty Gallery, Ann Zhao assembled a 20-something-page chapbook of sparks of inspiration and life dumps. A photo of her laptop on the couch, a screenshot of filmmaking notes, a snapshot of a few lines from a book—the content reads as if lifted from the artist’s social media or sketchpad, encapsulating the spontaneity that anchors her practice. That diaristic quality structures Ben Ming Nian (2026), 24 photographs from the year Zhao spent in Shanghai. The images fall just short of being autobiographical: opaque in their details and too fragmentary to cohere into narrative. She seems to leave the work unresolved, suspended on the threshold of completion.

article_text:
One of the greatest artists of the 20th century is coming to the big screen again from one of the 21st century’s true hyphenates.

Kid Cudi revealed on his Instagram on Wednesday that he will write, direct and star in a film about the life of Jean -Michel Basquiat.

“For years people have asked me about playing Jean Michel Basquiat in a film,” the Man on the Moon performer posted this morning. “But no project actually came to be. This year, I finally said f*ck it, ima write it myself.”

“This film will be a love letter to Jean, the 80s and NY city,” Cudi added of the acclaimed (and now bestselling) Basquiat, who died in 1988 at age 27. “Jean has inspired me all through out my career, and it will be the biggest honor to tell his story in a way we haven’t seen before.”

Jay Z & Apple Make It Official! Hova's Headlining The Super Bowl Halftime Show

The still-unreleased The Collaboration from director Kwame Kwei-Armah notwithstanding, it’s not like we haven’t seen a plethora of Basquiat documentaries and features over the decades.

Watch on Deadline

At the same time, with support from the likes of Jay-Z and other deep-pocket collectors, we’ve also seen Basquiat’s work rocket to the top of the sales charts. Not that Basquiat wasn’t successful during his lifetime, but that was nothing compared to what his paintings and other works rake in nowadays. In 2017, Basquiat’s Untitled from 1982 was sold for a then-record $110.5 million.

More recently, Andy Warhol and Jackson Pollack pieces have sold for more, but Basquiat remains a key and pricey American artist for collectors and museums.

In that context, not only did Grammy winner and Doe director Cudi (aka Scott Mescudi) unveil the “filming 2027” Jean , but also revealed some starling wardrobe takes of himself as Basquiat. No disrespect to Jeffrey Wright’s breakout performance in 1996’s Basquiat from Julian Schnabel, but Cudi clearly captures the essence of the artist — as the pics he posted show.

Already having announced a “horror/thriller” sophomore directorial feature in August, Cudi faced backlash last month after appearing onstage in Chicago with old pal Kanye West . In response, Cudi defended himself and to some degree West, who among antisemitic statements and other controversies released a pro-Hitler song last year.

“He was dealing w mental health struggles for years and now he’s good,” Cudi posted in the early hours of September 4. “Everyone deserves some grace when they family. I was the hardest on him out of anybody. I held him accountable. He apologized and it was sincere.”

On the flip side, Cudi was quick to cut M.I.A. loose in May from his tour in support of his Free album. At the Dallas stop of the tour, M.I.A. complained about being “canceled for being a brown Republican voter,” and then added, “I can’t do ‘illegal,’ though some of you could be in the audience.”

Cudi said in the aftermath: “I didn’t want anything offensive at my shows,” and M.I.A was M.I.A.

Back on the big screen, we now know Cudi’s second film as a director is entitled Wrong Number. In production in L.A., the Cudi-penned project co-stars Mile End Kicks alum Barbie Ferreira as Deadline’s Matt Grober exclusively reported last month.

As for Jean , take a look at Cudi’s post from today below.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Cohen Media Group will release its latest pic Everybody Digs Bill Evans starring Anders Danielsen Lie , Bill Pullman and Laurie Metcalf on December 4 in an Oscar-qualifying run at New York City’s The Quad ahead of a wider release beginning January 9, 2027.

The distributor will also submit Pullman for Best Supporting Actor, Metcalf for Best Supporting Actress and Lie for Best Actor in awards-season races.

Check out the first trailer above for the movie, which scored Grant Gee a Silver Bear for Directing at this year’s Berlin Film Festival, where it world premiered in competition.

Related Stories

‘Everybody Digs Bill Evans’ Review: Grant Gee’s Experimental Biopic Brings A Troubled Jazz Genius Hauntingly Back To Life – Berlin Film Festival

Anders Danielsen Lie, Bill Pullman & Laurie Metcalf To Star In ‘Everybody Digs Bill Evans’ About Seminal Jazz Pianist; Mister Smith & CAA Media Finance Launching For AFM

Lie plays legendary real-life jazz pianist Bill Evans in the unconventional biopic. It follows Evans’ decline after the 1961 car-crash death of his trio’s bass player Scott LaFaro soon after they recorded their seminal album Sunday at the Village Vanguard .

Watch on Deadline

Pullman and Metcalf play Evans’ parents, retirees in Florida who take in Bill, numb with grief, as he attempts to slow a spiral that includes heroin addition and quitting jazz. Barry Ward, Valene Kane and Katie McGrath also star.

The pic was adapted by Mark O’Halloran from Owen Martell’s novel Intermission . Janine Marmot and Alan Maher are producers.

After its debut screening in Berlin, Deadline’s Damon Wise in his review called the film “extraordinary, intimate and gloriously experimental.”

It has been on the festival circuit every since, including at the just-concluded Mill Valley (CA) Film Festival. Next up is the Middleburg Film Festival in Virginia which runs today-October 18.

article_text:
Note: This review was originally published as part of our 2026 NYFF coverage. The film opens in theaters on October 9.

Misty Green is a disaster on all fronts. It’s a film that seems to hate its characters, the audience, and Black cinema in general. It’s a Hollywood satire with no insight. It’s a character study with no character. It’s a drama uninterested in its own stakes. It’s a comedy unconcerned with making us laugh. The longer you watch it, the more it seems to only exist as a platform for writer-director Chris Rock’s most hateful impulses. The titular actress is a cipher, shepherded from scene to scene by plot mechanisms alone. Rosalind Eleazar plays Misty Green with energy and commitment, but the narrative has no real respect for her as a woman. The real star of the film is Rock himself, who plays a hapless director mysteriously named Jordan Green. He even shares his name with Misty’s mentally ill brother, referred to as Jay presumably to lessen confusion. But like most of the problems in the film, this needless misunderstanding can be attributed to Rock’s shocking lack of imagination. Going by Rock’s script, the most important thing to know about Misty Green is that she lets men down.

But who is Misty? The film never tells us, but it does provide some first-draft details. She grew up with a white mother and absent Black father. Her brother Jay (Daniel Kaluuya) isn’t her mother’s son, but she took him in anyway, and the three lived together unhappily. Misty has an Emmy for Best Supporting Actress in a Drama for her role in Red Eye , a fictional Shondaland series that used to come on after Scandal in the 2010s. Since then she has been financially supporting her brother while (presumably) spending the rest of her network checks on clothes, shoes, bags, and partying. When we meet her, she’s living in an apartment bought for her by a married man. It’s a year after his death and the widow (Amy Landecker) has come to seize the property. This dilemma gives Misty a ticking clock that she immediately ignores, partying with Zach (Adam Driver) the night before her audition. When she arrives late and unprepared the next morning, she ducks into a bathroom for a bump.

Making this situation all the more bleak is that Misty seems, at no point, to ever have any fun in her wild life. Everything she does is framed as a form of self-harm. Her only sex scene—with Zach—is passionless, her eyes looking forward as he hammers into her. She’s a lonely, pathetic character for seemingly no other reason than Rock needing her to be. It’s as if she’s based on a woman Rock fell for years ago but never really got to know. Perhaps he, like his director avatar, sees himself as a good man constantly set aside for reasons he’ll never fully understand. Regardless of how little Rock knows Misty, he knows her well enough to believe she should be punished. His film is the chronicle of a downfall unmotivated by any narrative truth beyond the fact that it’s what he wanted to film.

Throughout Misty Green , people ask Eleazar’s character if she knows any personal details about the people she considers friends. These repeated exchanges are meant to illustrate that Misty is a brat who only cares about herself. She struts through life in sexy clothes, Birkin bag in hand, with big eyes that always seem to be asking for a favor. She drinks only to get drunk. Her energy seems to come solely from cocaine. She smokes weed and cigarettes, rarely eats, and never seems to get enough sleep. The only healthy practice Misty manages to keep up with is going to her local gym with her best friend Naomi (Anna Kendrick). But even that is framed as an extension of Misty’s constant pursuit of unbridled vanity. Rock structures her story as a grim procession of humbling encounters, meant to bring her back down to Earth. It’s made all the more obvious by Rock’s constant onscreen presence, his character functioning as both a love interest and paternal figure. Misty Green is a woman’s story told entirely in a man’s voice, and that voice seems to hate her on a level that feels intensely personal and perverse.

Misty Green has no interest in the plight of Black women in Hollywood or their work, handwaving sexism and racism as if they’re both beside the point. This is also exemplified in the roles we see Misty read for and discuss. She is, for some reason, auditioning for the role played by N’Bushe Wright in the 1994 crime film Fresh . The sides she reads are direct quotes. If it were a reboot, why is the script the same? Later, we see an old clip of Misty reading for Anne Hathaway’s role in The Devil Wears Prada , which seems unrealistic based on her fame level. Throughout the journey we also hear about an ill-fated Cinderella reboot that brings to mind the 1997 version with Brandy Norwood and the late Whitney Houston. Then we hear about Misty being in Shaft —presumably the 2019 version, based on her age. But the biggest indication of Rock’s limited knowledge of recent roles for Black women is the part Misty chases the most throughout the film: Deena in Dreamgirls , last played in the 2006 film by Beyoncé. Though it is normal to reboot a film 20 years later, it seems unlikely that a television actress would be reading for a role previously played by one of the biggest singers on the planet.

If this suggests nitpicking, the laziness is distracting. The film’s one true invention, Red Eye , is a show no one takes the time to describe. Did Rock choose a title and immediately move on? Misty has an Emmy for playing a popular character, but no one mentions who that character was or even what she did on the show. The film is more concerned with the men in Misty’s life—especially her brother—and the many ways she has let them all down. As Misty’s life implodes around her, Rock pulls focus towards the unhoused residents of Los Angeles. Characters express disgust at having to see them on a constant basis, living in tents and asking for change. These moments, coupled with Misty’s money troubles, seem to function as a narrative threat. It’s as if Rock is saying that holding onto money is everything, and if you lose it, you become a nuisance and drain on society. The ending is especially tasteless in that regard. But perhaps California Governor Gavin Newsom will enjoy it.

Many will laud the work of Eleazar, who simply isn’t given a real character to play here. We never get into Misty’s head beyond flashbacks involving her brother. She often looks at a framed photograph of them with her mother, each close-up emptier than the last. Eleazar moves through every scene stiffly, her clothes fitting perfectly, her hair thick and luminous, her eyes begging for one more shot. But she never seems comfortable in the role, delivering her lines unconvincingly; audition and performance scenes are distinctly unnatural. This becomes especially clear in her scenes with Kendrick, who makes a meal out of a deeply troubled, darkly funny character. As for Kaluuya: he does the best he can with a poorly written role that turns him into a walking plot device. But it’s Rock’s performance as a scumbag deluded enough to think he’s a good guy that truly dooms the film. There is no good here. Misty Green is a black hole.

Misty Green screened at the 64th New York Film Festival and opens in theaters on October 9.

article_text:
In a scene that could have been ripped out of Stanley Kubrick’s Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb , a historic floor globe used by General Dwight D. Eisenhower during World War II was broken when Pentagon staff tried to move it, according to The Washington Post .

As reported by the paper, the globe caught the eye of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who ordered for it to be moved into his office to ogle on his own.

“Ordinarily, moving historical items within the building is a deliberate process overseen by trained curators,” the Post reported. “Instead, Hegseth’s staff dispatched its own team to relocate an Eisenhower globe. They lost control of the artifact and dropped it, sending the globe crashing onto its base and impaling the fragile shell near Antarctica, according to those familiar with the incident. The resulting gash appears to be several inches wide.”

The Pentagon did not provide access to the globe, but the Post obtained photographs that show extensive damage to the treasure that dates back to the 1930s. In addition to the hole in the would-be planet’s crust, Pentagon spokesman Christopher Surridge told the Post that “the spherical portion of the globe was detached from the metal mounting that allows it to rotate.”

After publication of the report this morning, the Defense Department provided an unattributed statement related to the globe. As the Post recounted: “‘Accidents happen,’ it says, ‘we are grateful no one was harmed, and the globe is being repaired.’ The statement does not say how much the repairs are expected to cost and when they would be complete.”
excerpt_original: Damage was incurred when trying to move it into the defense secretary's office.

article_text:
Iranian filmmaker Mohammad Rasoulof and Iranian-born Afghan director Shahrbanoo Sadat pushed back on the idea of a standalone Oscar category for exiled filmmakers, speaking at the Tokyo International Film Festival as Cate Blanchett ’s Displacement Film Fund gave its first five short films their Japan premiere.

The question followed the Academy’s recent rule change making exiled filmmakers eligible for the Oscars. The Academy’s top leadership was present at the festival this week.

Spotify Hums Along in Q3, Reaching 306 Million Paid Subscribers: 'There Is More Runway Ahead'

“I really do not like to be labeled, and even this label is displaced, you know, because I’m not seeing myself like I’m Shahrbanoo Sadat, the displaced filmmaker. This is funny, this is a joke to me,” said Sadat, whose fund-backed short is “Super Afghan Gym.” “I’m not sure if I would love to be in the category of displaced, even if they give me the Oscar.”

Rasoulof, who directed the fund’s “The Sense of Water,” said that as a filmmaker he wanted to put all his energy into making films, and that from that point of view it might not matter much where they are shown. “If there are certain specific categories, then sometimes those could cause an issue, so I would really like to focus my efforts on closing the distance and being closer,” he said.

Clare Stewart, managing director of International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR), whose Hubert Bals Fund manages the Displacement Film Fund, pointed out that Rasoulof’s own “The Seed of the Sacred Fig,” nominated in the last Oscar cycle, was one of the first films to benefit from the change, and that it represented Germany.

“And then what does that mean? What dialogue does that create? How does that open up our thinking more broadly about what the position of a displaced filmmaker or refugee filmmaker is in our social fabric?” Stewart said. “So I personally don’t feel there’s a need.”

Blanchett, the fund’s co-founder, said everyone on the panel had welcomed the Academy’s ruling and the way it acknowledged the real situation facing artists around the world. “There’s so many wars and conflicts, and people displaced through no fault of their own, and often careers, artistic careers are interrupted. So the fact that the Academy is recognizing that, I think is, it sounds like a small thing, but it is very profound,” she said.

The first cohort’s films have already had an Academy qualifying screening in Los Angeles, Blanchett said, with another set for New York in mid-November. “Of course for Academy considerations, but first and foremost so that yet another territory, the American territory, can see these extraordinary films,” she said.

“I don’t want to be too trivial, but the film industry is very used to international co-productions,” Blanchett added. “The cultural diplomacy that happens within our own industry, I wish a lot of governments would model the same level of communication.”

The fund backs filmmakers who are displaced themselves or who have a track record of telling authentic stories about displacement. It took shape at the UNHCR’s Global Refugee Forum in December 2023, where Blanchett, a UNHCR goodwill ambassador for more than a decade, first met Yanai Koji, a director and senior executive officer at Uniqlo parent Fast Retailing.

“When one in 70 people around the world is displaced, Koji-san and I and the other people at the Refugee Forum, including UNHCR, were saying, why aren’t these stories more in the mainstream? Why aren’t we talking about them? And it’s a chance to dispel the toxic narrative that is often around displaced persons’ experience,” Blanchett said.

Stewart said the effort gathered pace in October 2024, when she told Blanchett about the Hubert Bals Fund, which IFFR has run for 30 years to support filmmakers in countries where infrastructure is thin or where getting a film backed is politically difficult. IFFR signed on to manage the new fund, which launched at the festival in January 2025. Its founding partners are Yanai’s production company Mastermind, Uniqlo, the Tamer Family Foundation, the Amahoro Coalition and Dutch foundation Droom en Daad. The SP Lohia Foundation came aboard as a main partner at IFFR this year.

The first cohort, unveiled at Cannes in 2025, comprises Rasoulof, Sadat, Mo Harawe, Hasan Kattan and Maryna Er Gorbach. Their films premiered at IFFR in January and have also screened in London and El Gouna, with São Paulo on the festival run as well. A second cohort is now making its films . Blanchett said the filmmakers were given full freedom over subject and point of view, and their stories did not have to address displacement directly.

“The Sense of Water” centers on a migrant’s solitude and the struggle to learn a new language. “Three years ago, I had no choice but to flee my hometown and seek refuge overseas. There I had a sense of isolation, and I began to question this sense of isolation, wanting to understand where that would come from,” Rasoulof said.

Sadat was born in Iran to parents who fled the Soviet-Afghan War in 1979, moved at age 11 to a small village in central Afghanistan, and was evacuated to France and then Germany when Afghanistan collapsed. The fund approached her while she was editing “No Good Men,” a romantic comedy in which she ended up playing the lead after her actor withdrew three weeks before the shoot. That film opened the Berlin Film Festival and is set for release in Japan next year.

“I wanted to talk about these feelings of not being comfortable in your first and last home: your body,” Sadat said of “Super Afghan Gym.”

Japanese star Yakusho Koji, Cannes best actor winner for “Perfect Days,” a collaborator on Uniqlo’s Peace for All charity T-shirt project, was the surprise guest at a post-screening talk and described “The Sense of Water” as “a very quiet, calm film about love and hardships and deep hurt.” Sadat’s gym-set film, he said, “really brought a smile to my face.” Sadat said she only realized the film was being read as a comedy when critics called it one after its Rotterdam premiere.

Blanchett had a question of her own for Yakusho: “When are we going to work together?”
excerpt_original: Iranian filmmaker Mohammad Rasoulof and Iranian-born Afghan director Shahrbanoo Sadat pushed back on the idea of a standalone Oscar category for exiled filmmakers, speaking at the Tokyo International Film Festival as Cate Blanchett’s Displacement Film Fund gave its first five…

title_original: 討／逃海之後，回返母親的潮水──專訪《黑潮》導演池家慶
title_zh: 討／逃海之後，回返母親的潮水──專訪《黑潮》導演池家慶
summary_zh: 来源摘录：《黑潮》照見晦暗現實裡的邊緣人群，與「如何生」、「何以生」之間的徒勞。電影終幕為觀眾留下想像的空間，也似是池家慶給予角色的一絲溫柔。然而，我們能否以如此樂觀的心態，看待雪虹和阿忠的相遇，並稱其為「暗裡有光」，一種（可能的）救贖？池家慶回擲問題：阿忠最後的選擇，是對社會的恨，還是自我的放逐？ 這篇文章 討／逃海之後，回返母親的潮水──專訪《黑潮》導演池家慶 最早出現於 釀電影 。
